questions.question: In 2025, which new category was added by the Central Pollution Control Board to classify essential environmental services?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** introduced a new classification category named **Blue** in 2025 to identify and monitor essential environmental services.
 
• This classification aims to emphasize industries and services that have a **minimal environmental impact** while playing a crucial role in environmental preservation and sustainability.
 
• Such services include **water purification plants, renewable energy services, and waste management systems** that actively contribute to environmental conservation.
 
• The CPCB categorized industries and services based on their pollution index. The newly introduced **Blue category** represents activities with an index of **less than 10**, indicating negligible environmental harm.
 
• This initiative aligns with India’s commitment to achieving **sustainable development goals (SDGs)** and addressing climate change challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pollution Index Categories by CPCB:**

 
 
• Industries are classified into four categories based on their pollution index: **Red, Orange, Green, and Blue**.
 
• The **Red category** includes industries with a pollution index greater than 60, representing the highest pollution potential.
 
• The **Orange category** covers industries with a pollution index between 41 and 59, posing moderate pollution risks.
 
• The **Green category** includes industries with a pollution index between 21 and 40, indicating low pollution potential.
 
• The newly added **Blue category** includes industries and services with a pollution index of less than 10, emphasizing negligible environmental impact.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Blue Category Services:**
 
 
• **Water purification plants** that ensure clean and safe drinking water.
 
• **Renewable energy services** like solar and wind energy production, which support eco-friendly energy solutions.
 
• **Waste management systems** that include recycling, composting, and waste-to-energy conversion.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The classification of industries into pollution categories aligns with global efforts to achieve the **United Nations’ SDG 13** (Climate Action) and **SDG 6** (Clean Water and Sanitation).
 
• Blue category services actively contribute to reducing environmental degradation and promoting sustainable practices.
 
 
 
• **Importance of CPCB’s Role:**
 
 
• The **CPCB** is India’s principal body for controlling pollution and ensuring environmental regulations are implemented effectively.
 
• Its classification system helps in monitoring and regulating industrial activities while promoting cleaner and greener alternatives.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Blue Category Threshold:**

 
 
• The pollution index for the Blue category is **less than 10**, ensuring that the classified services and industries have almost no adverse environmental impact.
 
 
 
• **Global Environmental Commitment:**
 
 
• India is a signatory to the **Paris Agreement** and other international environmental treaties, which emphasize reducing pollution and promoting sustainability.
 
• The introduction of the Blue category reflects India’s proactive approach to fulfilling its environmental responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **CPCB Guidelines:**
 
 
• The CPCB provides detailed guidelines for industries and services to minimize their environmental impact and comply with pollution control norms.
 
• Industries in the Blue category are encouraged to adopt **innovative, eco-friendly technologies**.

questions.question: Which of the following two countries exchanged prisoners of war in Istanbul in June 2025?

• In June 2025, a **prisoner exchange agreement** was facilitated through efforts involving third-party mediators, including Turkey, which has played a neutral role in the conflict.
 
• The prisoner exchange occurred in **Istanbul, Turkey**, a country that has consistently offered to mediate peace talks between the two nations.
 
• This exchange involved the release of **captured soldiers and civilians** from both sides, aiming to reduce humanitarian concerns and build trust for future negotiations.
 
• Such exchanges are part of broader **confidence-building measures** to de-escalate tensions, even as the larger conflict remains unresolved.

• The conflict began in 2014 when Russia annexed **Crimea** and supported separatist movements in eastern Ukraine (Donetsk and Luhansk regions).
 
• The war escalated in February 2022 when Russia launched a **full-scale invasion** of Ukraine, leading to widespread destruction and a humanitarian crisis.
 
 
 
• **Role of Turkey in Mediating:**
 
 
• Turkey, under the leadership of **President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan**, has maintained diplomatic relations with both Russia and Ukraine.
 
• Istanbul has served as a key location for peace negotiations and humanitarian exchanges due to Turkey's neutral stance.
 
 
 
• **Humanitarian Impact of the Conflict:**
 
 
• Millions of people have been displaced, with over **8 million Ukrainian refugees** seeking asylum in various European countries.
 
• Prisoner exchanges, like the one in Istanbul, are crucial for addressing the plight of **captured soldiers and civilians**.
 
 
 
• **Prisoner Exchange Agreements:**
 
 
• Such agreements are often brokered through third-party mediators or international organizations like the **United Nations** or the **International Committee of the Red Cross** (ICRC).
 
• The exchange includes **clear identification** and verification processes to ensure the safe return of individuals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geopolitical Significance of Istanbul:**

 
 
• Istanbul, located at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, has historically been a hub for **international diplomacy**.
 
• It serves as a neutral ground for talks involving contentious parties like Russia and Ukraine.
 
 
 
• **Confidence-Building Measures:**
 
 
• Prisoner exchanges are often seen as a step toward initiating broader peace talks.
 
• Such measures help to reduce tensions and address **humanitarian concerns**.
 
 
 
• **Global Reactions:**

questions.question: In which city did the Union Home Minister launch the pilot project of the e-Zero FIR initiative in May 2025, under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to improve the efficiency of investigating cyber financial frauds, supporting the vision of a Cyber Secure Bharat?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Union Home Minister launched the pilot project of the **e-Zero FIR initiative** in **Delhi** in **May 2025** under the **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C).**
 
• This initiative is aimed at improving the efficiency of investigating **cyber financial frauds** and aligns with the vision of a **Cyber Secure Bharat.**
 
• The **e-Zero FIR** allows victims to lodge a First Information Report (FIR) online without visiting a police station, streamlining the process for addressing cybercrime complaints.
 
• The selection of **Delhi** as the launch city highlights its role as a central hub for technology and administration, making it a suitable choice for piloting innovative cybercrime solutions.
 
• The **I4C** initiative is a flagship program of the Ministry of Home Affairs, aimed at tackling the increasing challenges posed by cybercrime through coordination and advanced technological tools.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C):**

 
 
• I4C was established in **2018** under the Ministry of Home Affairs to act as a nodal agency to deal with all types of cybercrime in India.
 
• The center facilitates coordination among different states and union territories, providing advanced technologies and training to tackle cybercrimes.
 
• It includes components such as a **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, Cyber Forensic Laboratory, and Cyber Training Centre.**
 
 
 
• **Cyber Financial Frauds:**
 
 
• Cyber financial frauds include crimes like **phishing, identity theft, credit card frauds, online scams, and unauthorized transactions.**
 
• These crimes have increased significantly with the growth of digital transactions and require advanced tools and frameworks like the **e-Zero FIR initiative** for effective investigation and resolution.
 
 
 
• **FIR (First Information Report):**
 
 
• An FIR is a written document prepared by the police when they receive information about the commission of a cognizable offense.
 
• The **e-Zero FIR initiative** allows individuals to file FIRs online, reducing the need for physical visits to police stations and expediting the process.
 
 
 
• **Cyber Secure Bharat Vision:**
 
 
• The vision of a **Cyber Secure Bharat** aims to create a safe and secure digital environment for citizens, businesses, and government entities.
 
• It includes initiatives like **cyber literacy campaigns, technological advancements, and improved legal frameworks** to combat cybercrime.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Delhi:**

 
 
• Delhi, being the capital city, serves as a hub for technological infrastructure and administrative coordination, making it an ideal location for pilot projects like the **e-Zero FIR initiative.**
 
• It houses several government offices, research institutions, and cybersecurity units, providing logistical advantages for implementing such projects.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements:**
 
 
• Projects like **e-Zero FIR** reflect the government's commitment to leveraging **technology** to address modern challenges, especially in the domain of **cybersecurity.**
 
• Such advancements help in reducing delays and improving transparency in the investigation process.

questions.question: What is the surplus amount transferred by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to the Centre for FY25?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹2.69 lakh crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** has transferred a surplus amount of **₹2.69 lakh crore** to the central government for the financial year 2024-25 (FY25).
 
• This transfer represents a significant increase compared to previous years, reflecting robust earnings, including from investments in government securities and foreign exchange operations.
 
• The surplus amount is transferred under the provisions of the **RBI Act, 1934**, which mandates the transfer of surplus profits after meeting the contingency reserve requirements.
 
• The increase in surplus transfer can be attributed to factors such as higher interest income on domestic and foreign investments, effective forex reserve management, and reduced expenditure by the RBI.
 
• Such a transfer plays a crucial role in the central government’s fiscal management, providing additional resources for public spending, reducing fiscal deficit, and funding welfare schemes.
 
• The decision on the surplus transfer is made annually by the RBI’s Central Board of Directors based on the recommendations of the Economic Capital Framework (ECF).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **RBI Surplus Transfer Mechanism**:

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is required to transfer its surplus profits to the central government under Section 47 of the **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• The surplus is calculated after meeting all expenses, including operational costs, provisions for contingency funds, and maintaining a sufficient reserve buffer.
 
• In 2019, the RBI adopted a revised **Economic Capital Framework (ECF)** based on the recommendations of the Bimal Jalan Committee to determine the appropriate level of reserves to be maintained by the central bank.
 
• The ECF ensures a balance between retaining sufficient reserves for financial stability and transferring excess profits to the government.
 
 
 
• **Key Components of RBI’s Income**:
 
 
• **Interest income**: Derived from government securities, foreign currency assets, and other investments.
 
• **Foreign exchange operations**: Profits from buying and selling foreign currencies.
 
• **Fees and commissions**: Income from banking services provided to the government and other entities.
 
• **Other income**: Includes penalties, grants, or miscellaneous revenue.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Surplus Transfer on Economy**:
 
 
• The surplus transfer provides an additional fiscal cushion to the government, helping in reducing the fiscal deficit.
 
• It supports increased spending on development projects, infrastructure, and welfare schemes, boosting economic growth.
 
• However, a higher transfer could also raise concerns about the central bank’s financial autonomy and its ability to manage contingencies.
 
 
 
• **Historical Trends in RBI Surplus Transfer**:
 
 
• In FY21, the RBI transferred a surplus of **₹99,122 crore**, while in FY22, it transferred **₹30,307 crore**.
 
• The sharp rise in FY25’s transfer to **₹2.69 lakh crore** is attributed to increased earnings from domestic and foreign operations.
 
• The adoption of the revised ECF has also streamlined the calculation of surplus, ensuring transparency and consistency.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bimal Jalan Committee Report**:

 
 
• Formed in 2018, this committee was tasked with reviewing the RBI’s economic capital framework.
 
• It recommended maintaining the RBI’s reserves within a range of **5.5%-6.5%** of its balance sheet.
 
• The framework ensures that surplus transfers do not compromise the central bank’s ability to handle financial or external shocks.
 
 
 
• **Economic Implications of Fiscal Deficit Reduction**:
 
 
• Higher surplus transfers can help the government reduce its fiscal deficit, leading to lower borrowing requirements.
 
• Reduced fiscal deficit strengthens investor confidence and enhances India’s credit rating.
 
• However, excessive reliance on surplus transfers could limit the RBI’s ability to address potential economic crises.

questions.question: Which of the following athletes was NOT part of the Indian 4 times 100 m relay team that set a new national record at the National Relay Carnival, 2025?

• **Neeraj Chopra** is primarily known for his achievements in the sport of javelin throw, including his gold medal win at the **Tokyo Olympics 2020**, making him one of India's most successful track and field athletes.
 
• Relay teams consist of four sprinters who specialize in running short distances and are trained for baton exchanges, a key component of relay races. Neeraj Chopra's expertise lies in the javelin throw, which is a field event, not a track relay event.
 
• The inclusion of sprinters like **Animesh Kujur, Manikanta Hoblidar**, and **Amlan Borgohain** in the relay team highlights their competence and specialization in the track events, whereas **Neeraj Chopra**'s absence is in line with his focus on field events.

questions.question: What is the name of (India) Bharat’s First Anti-Pesticide Bodysuit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kisan Kavach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kisan Kavach** is the name of **India's first anti-pesticide bodysuit**, designed to protect farmers from harmful pesticide exposure while working in agricultural fields.
 
• This bodysuit has been specially developed to address the challenges faced by Indian farmers, such as exposure to toxic chemicals during pesticide spraying.
 
• The suit acts as a protective shield, ensuring that harmful pesticides do not come into direct contact with the farmer's skin, thereby reducing health risks.
 
• It is made from lightweight and durable materials, ensuring comfort and ease of movement while providing robust protection.
 
• Such innovations are crucial for improving the working conditions of farmers and safeguarding their health, contributing to the larger goal of sustainable agricultural practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Anti-Pesticide Bodysuits:**

 
 
• Farmers in India often work in hazardous conditions, with exposure to harmful pesticides leading to severe health issues such as respiratory problems, skin diseases, and even long-term ailments like cancer.
 
• The anti-pesticide bodysuit, like **Kisan Kavach**, provides a preventive solution, reducing the likelihood of pesticide-related health complications.
 
• Such suits are particularly valuable in states with intensive agricultural activities, such as Punjab, Haryana, and Maharashtra, where pesticide use is prevalent.
 
 
 
• **Features of Kisan Kavach:**
 
 
• Made from advanced, non-toxic materials that resist pesticide penetration.
 
• Lightweight and breathable design to ensure comfort in hot and humid conditions.
 
• Reusable and cost-effective, making it affordable for farmers across different economic strata.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for Farmer Safety:**
 
 
• The government has initiated awareness campaigns and training programs to educate farmers about the risks of pesticide exposure and the importance of using protective gear.
 
• Subsidies and financial assistance are being provided to encourage the adoption of safety equipment, including bodysuits like **Kisan Kavach**.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like the USA and Japan have long adopted protective gear for farmers to mitigate pesticide exposure, serving as a model for similar initiatives in India.
 
• With the introduction of **Kisan Kavach**, India is taking significant steps toward aligning with global standards in agricultural safety.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Health Risks of Pesticides:**

 
 
• Pesticides contain harmful chemicals such as organophosphates, carbamates, and pyrethroids, which can cause acute poisoning and long-term health issues.
 
• Symptoms of pesticide poisoning include nausea, dizziness, headache, and skin irritation, with severe cases leading to organ damage or death.
 
 
 
• **Role of Technology in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Innovations like anti-pesticide bodysuits, drones for spraying pesticides, and AI-powered monitoring systems are transforming traditional farming practices in India.
 
• These advancements contribute to sustainable agriculture by minimizing health risks, improving efficiency, and reducing environmental damage.
 
 
 
• **Future Scope:**
 
 
• Scaling up the production of anti-pesticide bodysuits like **Kisan Kavach** can ensure widespread availability and affordability for farmers.
 
• Collaborations between the government, private sector, and research institutions can lead to further innovations in farmer safety equipment.
